parts.text: To make lift, an aircraft wing is angled to the airflow. This is called the angle of attack. As the speed of the aircraft decreases, the angle of attack, a°, increases to get more lift. The amount of lift depends on a quantity known as the lift coefficient, C. This table shows how C changes for different values of the angle of attack. Angle of attack (a° ) -5 0 5 10 15 20 25 Lift coefficient (C ) 0.00 0.55 1.05 1.46 1.70 1.66 1.44 A possible model for C is ( ) C m n a 17 2 = + - where m and n are constants.

An aircraft has a wing area of \(125m^{2}\) . It flies \(\bullet\) at a height of 12km above sea level \(\bullet\) at a speed of 210m/s \(\bullet\) with angle of attack \(3^{\circ}.\)
